event.description: What happened, as the source says it.

days_ago.description: Calendar days from date to now's date, computed (step 5); at most lookback_days.

matches.description: The rubric signals this event matches, copied exactly. Only when a rubric was given.

verdict.description: Absent only for a skipped slot.

rubric_score.description: 10 x weight of matched rubric signals / total weight, rounded half up. Only when a rubric was given.

dropped.description: Evidence items left out, by reason. Each non-zero count is also a line in report.unknowns.

off_rubric.description: Specific events that matched no rubric signal. Only when a rubric was given.

already_reported.description: Events the previous run already reported. Only with track_state.

item_result.title: Per-item result
item_result.description: What a per-item judge skill returns next to its own fields, so results-rank can combine the branches of any fan-out agent. Copied into properties.item_result of each output schema that has an item_result property.

item.description: The item judged, echoed from the slot it came from. Null for a skipped (empty) slot.

item_key.description: The stable identity key list-prepare gave this item (e.g. domain:acme.example, email:jo@acme.example). Copied unchanged. Memory, de-duplication across runs and later agents join on it. Empty only for a skipped slot.

item_label.description: How to name the item in a list, e.g. 'Acme (acme.example)'. Empty for a skipped slot.

status.description: skipped = the slot was empty; no_evidence = judged, but nothing usable was found. A failed branch is detected by the platform, not reported here.

verdict.description: The skill's own verdict word, e.g. Pursue, Research, Reject.

score.description: The skill's own score; score_scale gives its range.

source_ids.description: Ids in this skill's report.sources that back the headline.

report.title: Channel-neutral report
report.description: What every task skill returns for a human to read. channel-message-render turns it into a Slack, Teams, Discord, email or markdown payload. Every citation id must resolve to an entry in sources, and every source url must appear verbatim in the evidence the skill was given.

summary.description: One-paragraph TL;DR in plain text. Empty only when there is nothing to report.

severity.description: Drives color and emphasis in rendering. action_needed only when the reader must do something.

body_md.description: Optional prose under the heading. Basic markdown only: bold, italic, links, bullet lists.

citations.description: Ids from sources. Empty only for items that make no factual claim (e.g. a recommendation).

label.description: Short tag such as a verdict or category, e.g. Pursue, funding.

url.description: The web address exactly as it appears in the evidence. For pasted text, input:<field>.

record_ref.description: For an API record with no web address (enrichment, CRM, transcript): <provider>:<kind>/<id>, e.g. apollo:person/5f2a. The id must appear in the evidence exactly as given.

published_at.description: ISO 8601 date or datetime when the source states one; omit when unknown, never guess.

provider.description: Which tool returned it, when known (tavily, exa, brave, firecrawl, serpapi, perplexity, github, apollo, peopledatalabs, crustdata, fireflies, gong, granola, input).

sources.description: Every cited source. Each has a url, a record_ref, or both.

unknowns.description: What could not be established, and why. A first-class result, not a failure.

meta.description: Who produced this report and when, so another agent that reads it later knows what it is reading.

generated_at.description: The run's `now` input (ISO 8601). Never invent a time.

state_out.title: State to remember
state_out.description: What a skill that compares over time asks the agent to save for the next run. Copied into properties.state_out of each output schema that has a state_out property. The skill never saves it; a later write step does (Sheets, Notion, a memory connector, or platform memory once it exists).

fingerprint.description: A short, stable summary of what was observed (e.g. sorted event urls, a price string), compared on the next run to detect change.

data.description: Small extra fields the next run needs. Keep it under 2 KB.

state_sheet_values.description: Only with track_state: state_out.entries as spreadsheet cells: item_key, fingerprint, observed_at, data_json. null when there are no entries.
